name: Roland SH-32
description: Roland SH-32 virtual-analog synthesizer module: the temporary performance (common and all four parts) with Part 1's patch, and the Patch-mode patch and rhythm set, with the arpeggio and rhythm styles and chord forms of both modes, from the temporary (edit-buffer) area of the MIDI Implementation.

sources.title: SH-32 MIDI Implementation (version 1.00, Dec. 12, 2001)
sources.notes: Parameter Address Map read by tools/profiles/roland/parse-address-map.mjs from SH-32_MI.pdf (sha256 99575b06d7cd7a139a83c40dbf51c419bab5fd3524d77395108cf6dbd50b6a18). Model ID 00 4A, DT1 = 12, RQ1 = 11, Roland checksum. Not yet checked against the instrument itself.

authoringNotes: Generated by tools/profiles/roland/make-profiles.mjs; edit the layout in tools/profiles/roland/synths/, not this file.
Every parameter is the manual's, at the manual's address, with the manual's name. Nothing here has been sent to a real instrument yet.

Patch mode (14 00 00 00) holds a patch at 14 00 00 00 or a rhythm set at 14 10 00 00, the key blocks from 14 10 10 00 (key 21) to 14 11 3E 00 (key 108), all 88 laid out; both are read on request, not at connect.

Presets list the Patches and the user Rhythm Sets (p1). Performances (MSB 85, LSB 0; 64, 20 00 00 00 - 20 3F 00 00) are selected on the Performance Control Channel instead and are not listed. The preset Rhythm Sets (MSB 86, LSB 64: r3P and r4P, p6) are not listed either: the bank table prints no program numbers, and whether they are programs 1-2 or 3-4 of their bank is not said.

p12 <Example2> gives Patch "A11" a start address of 30 08 00 00 and requests F0 41 10 00 4A 11 30 08 00 00 00 00 12 0D 29 F7; the address map (p6) puts Patch (001 :A11) at 30 00 00 00 (30 08 00 00 is Patch 009, A21). It also introduces the patch's offsets as "the offset address of Rhythm".

p12 <Example3> names the rhythm set's blocks "Temporary Rhythm", "Rhythm Common", "Rhythm INS-FX", "Rhythm REV/DELAY" and "Rhythm Wave (Key # n)", and Part 1 "Temporary Patch/Rhythm (Performance Mode Part 1)"; the map (p6-7) prints Temporary Rhythm Set, Rhythm Set Common, Rhythm Set INS-FX, Rhythm Set REV/DELAY, Rhythm Tone (Key # n), and "Temporary Patch (Performance Mode Part 1)". Its message, F0 41 10 00 4A 11 10 00 00 00 01 71 3E 1E 22 F7, is consistent with the map.
The top table (p6) labels the second Rhythm Set "002 :r1U" (r2U) and the second Rhythm Style "067 :12.r" at 50 41 00 00 (066).
Performance Common Chord Form Select (00 19, p7) prints its range as "11.r - 88.r", the rhythm styles' names; Patch Common's Chord Form prints "11.c - 88.c". Both are kept as printed.
Arpeggio Style (Rhythm Style) (p9) prints the fourth grid step "Step4 Data" between "Grid 3 Data" and "Grid 5 Data"; it is kept as printed (arpeggioStyle.note1.step4Data).

Printed names kept as printed: "CC#1 Filter Cutcoff Sens" (Patch Common 00 17), "RETRIGER" (Legato Switch), "Pluse Wave Number" (Patch Oscillator 00 07), "HF DUMP/MOD RATE" (REV/DELAY 00 12). "CC#1 …" ids read cc1… (the # is "number").
The MIDI Implementation is dated Dec. 12, 2001 at its head (p1); the MIDI Implementation Chart that ends it (p13) is dated Oct. 30, 2001.

Not read at startup (read on request, since the instrument may not answer them): patch, patch.insFx, patch.revDelay, patch.osc1, patch.osc2, rhythm, rhythm.insFx, rhythm.revDelay, rhythm.key21, rhythm.key22, rhythm.key23, rhythm.key24, rhythm.key25, rhythm.key26, rhythm.key27, rhythm.key28, rhythm.key29, rhythm.key30, rhythm.key31, rhythm.key32, rhythm.key33, rhythm.key34, rhythm.key35, rhythm.key36, rhythm.key37, rhythm.key38, rhythm.key39, rhythm.key40, rhythm.key41, rhythm.key42, rhythm.key43, rhythm.key44, rhythm.key45, rhythm.key46, rhythm.key47, rhythm.key48, rhythm.key49, rhythm.key50, rhythm.key51, rhythm.key52, rhythm.key53, rhythm.key54, rhythm.key55, rhythm.key56, rhythm.key57, rhythm.key58, rhythm.key59, rhythm.key60, rhythm.key61, rhythm.key62, rhythm.key63, rhythm.key64, rhythm.key65, rhythm.key66, rhythm.key67, rhythm.key68, rhythm.key69, rhythm.key70, rhythm.key71, rhythm.key72, rhythm.key73, rhythm.key74, rhythm.key75, rhythm.key76, rhythm.key77, rhythm.key78, rhythm.key79, rhythm.key80, rhythm.key81, rhythm.key82, rhythm.key83, rhythm.key84, rhythm.key85, rhythm.key86, rhythm.key87, rhythm.key88, rhythm.key89, rhythm.key90, rhythm.key91, rhythm.key92, rhythm.key93, rhythm.key94, rhythm.key95, rhythm.key96, rhythm.key97, rhythm.key98, rhythm.key99, rhythm.key100, rhythm.key101, rhythm.key102, rhythm.key103, rhythm.key104, rhythm.key105, rhythm.key106, rhythm.key107, rhythm.key108.

coverage.inboundControllers: not modelled: what the knobs and the front panel transmit as CC (Data Transmission, p4-6) is not mapped yet
coverage.parts: the Temporary Performance (10 00 00 00) whole, and Part 1's temporary patch (11 00 00 00). Not laid out: Part 2's and Part 3's patches (11 20 00 00, 11 40 00 00) and Part 4's patch or rhythm set (11 60 00 00: the patch at +00 00 00, the rhythm set at +10 00 00, i.e. 11 70 00 00), each the same blocks as the Patch-mode patch and rhythm set laid out here
coverage.memories: not laid out: Performances 01-64 (20 00 00 00), Patches 001-128 (30 00 00 00), Rhythm Sets (40 00 00 00, 40 10 00 00), Arpeggio and Rhythm Styles (50 00 00 00 - 50 7F 00 00), Chord Forms (60 00 00 00 - 60 00 7E 00): memory rather than edit buffer
coverage.effectParameterMeanings: named: INS-FX (Intensity, Color, Rate, Level) and REV/DELAY (E.Level, Time, FBK, …) are four named parameters each, as printed (p8-9); what they do depends on the selected type, which the MIDI Implementation does not list
